REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JULY 8, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 815 6991 7087
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public subject to Los Angeles County mandated COVID-19 protocols. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will also be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below, or in-person subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using any of the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81569917087
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 815 6991 7087
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
JULY 8, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 815 6991 7087

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Reverend Dustin Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  None.

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Nashwaan Ali Khan and his associate spoke regarding the Connect Students Around the
  World Program and requested the City’s endorsement of their program in Bangladesh.
  He submitted written correspondence entitled, “Connect Students Around the World
  (CSAW) Proposal to Cerritos City Council,” for the record. (Written correspondence is
  considered public record and full-text copies of submitted written correspondence can be
  obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Angela Brunson urged the City Council to place an item to review and consider a Vote of
  No Confidence in Los Angeles County District Attorney George Gascón on an upcoming
  meeting agenda.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to place an item on a future
  agenda to review and consider a resolution expressing a Vote of No Confidence in Los
  Angeles County District Attorney George Gascón.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, June 24, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Thursday, June
  24, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated July 8, 2021 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  July 8, 2021  $2,416,405.36 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending May 31, 2021
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending May 31, 2021
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 6

  Vote to reorder items on the agenda

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to reorder items on the
  agenda by considering Item 9A prior to the consideration of Item 8A
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 3-2, to approve the
  following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING SECTION 22.48.600 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL
  CODE, ADDING AND CLARIFYING REGULATIONS FOR POLITICAL SIGNS, HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2021-1* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Celia Spitzer submitted written correspondence in support of the proposed ordinance
  adding and clarifying regulations for political signs.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  City Council and staff discussion ensued on this matter.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to return the subject ordinance
  related to adding and clarifying regulations for political signs to the Planning Commission for
  further consideration, inclusive of the comments received from the City Council during the
  public hearing (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of renaming Jacob Park in honor of former Cerritos Mayor and
  Councilmember Jim Edwards (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherrè Titus, Recreation Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Mike Lee submitted written correspondence in opposition to naming Jacob Park after
  former Mayor and City Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Sue Carter submitted written correspondence in support of renaming Jacob Park after
  former Mayor and City Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Audio public comments:

  Celena and Danny Morales spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor
  and City Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Roger Garrett spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Gloria Kappe spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Sherman Kappe spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Larry Sagert spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Clarence Stephens spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Emmett Hall spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Dr. Bob Hughlett spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Richard Martinez spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Laurie Forward spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Chan Yong Kim spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Alan Sahussanun spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  David Montgomery spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Anthony LeBlanc spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and City
  Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Desmond E. Thompson spoke in support of renaming Jacob Park after former Mayor and
  City Councilmember Jim Edwards.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to rename Jacob Park in
  honor of former Cerritos Mayor and Councilmember Jim Edwards (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were given by Councilmember Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem Vo, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to
  discuss the following items as listed on the Closed Session agenda:

  12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, July 8, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 6

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  12D.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to California Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of potential cases: 1

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session.

  The City Attorney, pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.1, reported out the City
  Council convened in Closed Session to discuss Items 12A, 12B, 12C, and 12D as listed
  on the agenda. The City Council conducted performance evaluations for the positions
  listed for Closed Session Items 12A (City Manager), 12B (City Attorney), and 12C (City
  Clerk/Treasurer), with no reportable action.

  With regard to Item 12D, the City Council took the following reportable action:

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to retain special counsel
  and join as a co-petitioner in Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No.
  21STCP01970, titled Orange County Council of Governments, Petitioner, v. Gustavo
  Velasquez, Interim Director for the California Department of Housing and Community
  Development (HCD) and HCD, Respondents, with Real Party in Interest Southern
  California Association of Governments (SCAG). In summary, the petition for writ of
  mandate seeks to set aside the regional housing needs allocation of dwelling units as
  determined by HCD for the SCAG region and to conduct a new allocation in compliance
  with state local planning laws (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 1:30 a.m. on Friday, July 9, 2021.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
